candidate_rule: two non-promoted evidence candidates per source: one verified fact and one scope limitation

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — full-fibre availability
sources.fact: As of January 2026, full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of the UK's 30.5 million homes, after a six-month increase of 1.2 million homes.
sources.scope_limit: This national availability statistic does not prove that a specific address can order a retail full-fibre service today.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — full-fibre take-up
sources.fact: Full-fibre take-up across UK residential and commercial premises increased by 1.8 million connections in six months to 12.4 million, corresponding to 47% of premises with access to full fibre.
sources.scope_limit: Take-up is an aggregate adoption measure and cannot identify the service status, provider or product at an individual parcel.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — gigabit-capable availability
sources.fact: Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 89%, or 27.1 million UK homes, up from 87% or 26.4 million homes in July 2025.
sources.scope_limit: National coverage percentages are not a substitute for current UPRN-level or provider orderability checks.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — affordable decent broadband gap
sources.fact: Ofcom reported only 4,000 premises without access to affordable decent broadband, mainly after lower-priced satellite services became available in selected areas.
sources.scope_limit: Affordability and satellite eligibility depend on location, price and product terms and do not prove fixed-network availability at a parcel.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — fixed-line or FWA gap
sources.fact: The number of premises unable to access decent broadband from fixed line or fixed wireless access fell to 39,000 from 44,000 in July 2025.
sources.scope_limit: The aggregate gap cannot identify which exact premises remain unserved or whether alternative satellite products are affordable.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — 4G geographic coverage
sources.fact: Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from all mobile network operators reached 84% of UK landmass, while coverage from at least one operator remained at 96%.
sources.scope_limit: Modelled geographic coverage is not an indoor signal, capacity or service-quality guarantee for a specific premises.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — 5G standalone coverage
sources.fact: Outside-premises 5G standalone coverage ranged from 49% to 85% across the three operators that had deployed 5G SA, compared with 47% to 65% in July 2025.
sources.scope_limit: High-confidence outdoor predictions do not establish indoor availability, handset compatibility or subscription eligibility at an address.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2026 — overall 5G coverage
sources.fact: Overall outside-premises 5G coverage for individual operators ranged from 76% to 94%, and coverage from all operators increased from 47% to 64%.
sources.scope_limit: The figures combine 5G standalone and non-standalone predictions and are not exact-address performance evidence.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations — Planned Network Deployments 2026: network overlap
sources.fact: Ofcom estimated that by the end of 2028, 73% of UK homes could have access to at least two gigabit-capable networks and 36% to at least three.
sources.scope_limit: Operator plans are forward-looking and do not prove completed build, activation or retail orderability at an exact address.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Connected Nations — Planned Network Deployments 2026: FWA mast plans
sources.fact: Operators planned or expected upgrades for about 6,950 additional geographically distinct fixed-wireless-access masts between January 2026 and January 2029.
sources.scope_limit: A planned mast upgrade does not establish line-of-sight, capacity, product availability or service at a particular parcel.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Telecommunications Market Data Update Q1 2026 — fixed broadband lines
sources.fact: There were 29.4 million UK fixed broadband lines at the end of Q1 2026, an increase of 282,000 or 1.0% year on year.
sources.scope_limit: Market line counts describe national subscriptions and do not reveal the access technology or availability at an individual premises.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML and linked official statistics; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Telecommunications Market Data Update Q1 2026 — active mobile subscriptions
sources.fact: Active mobile subscriptions excluding machine-to-machine connections reached 90.6 million at the end of Q1 2026, up 881,000 or 1.0% year on year.
sources.scope_limit: Subscription totals are market-size indicators and cannot establish network coverage or service quality at a parcel.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML and linked official statistics; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Telecommunications Market Data Update Q1 2026 — dedicated mobile broadband
sources.fact: Dedicated mobile broadband subscriptions increased by 421,000 or 8.8% year on year to 5.2 million in Q1 2026.
sources.scope_limit: National subscription growth does not prove that a particular address has adequate mobile broadband coverage or capacity.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML and linked official statistics; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Telecommunications Market Data Update Q1 2026 — mobile data usage
sources.fact: Mobile data volumes increased by 351 petabytes or 13.1% year on year to 3,042 petabytes in Q1 2026.
sources.scope_limit: Aggregate traffic growth does not measure local congestion, signal strength or achievable speed at an exact premises.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML and linked official statistics; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: Broadband complaints fall to record low
sources.fact: Ofcom reported six broadband complaints per 100,000 customers in Q1 2026, the lowest level in its series and down from a peak of 40 per 100,000 in 2011.
sources.scope_limit: Complaint rates measure reported dissatisfaction among major providers and do not establish service availability or quality at an individual address.
sources.attribution: Official Ofcom HTML; Ofcom attribution retained.

sources.title: July 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts — total
sources.fact: BDUK's 16 July 2026 management-information snapshot listed 838,490 initial-scope contracted premises and 287,510 built contracted premises across Project Gigabit contracts.
sources.scope_limit: The rounded contract-level snapshot has ingestion lag, excludes deferred scope and is not direct evidence of current exact-address orderability.
sources.attribution: Official GOV.UK HTML; Open Government Licence v3.0 attribution retained.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract — Bedfordshire, Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes redesign
sources.fact: BDUK and CityFibre redesigned the contract to cover around 6,000 premises backed by £19.8 million after commercial rollout expansion and market changes.
sources.scope_limit: Redesigned programme scope does not prove that a specific premises remains included, has been built or can order service.
sources.attribution: Official GOV.UK HTML; Open Government Licence v3.0 attribution retained.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract — Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East Berkshire redesign
sources.fact: BDUK and CityFibre redesigned the contract to around 6,000 premises backed by £24.4 million.
sources.scope_limit: The regional redesign is not a current UPRN-level inclusion, build-completion or retail-availability record.
sources.attribution: Official GOV.UK HTML; Open Government Licence v3.0 attribution retained.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract — Cambridgeshire redesign
sources.fact: BDUK and CityFibre redesigned the Cambridgeshire contract to around 35,000 premises backed by up to £77 million.
sources.scope_limit: A revised contract envelope does not prove exact-premises inclusion, completed infrastructure or an orderable product.
sources.attribution: Official GOV.UK HTML; Open Government Licence v3.0 attribution retained.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract — East and West Sussex redesign
sources.fact: BDUK and CityFibre redesigned the East and West Sussex contract to around 13,000 premises backed by £25.2 million.
sources.scope_limit: Regional programme scope cannot be promoted to exact-address connectivity without current UPRN and provider validation.
sources.attribution: Official GOV.UK HTML; Open Government Licence v3.0 attribution retained.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract — Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire ended
sources.fact: BDUK stated that CityFibre is no longer delivering the Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract and that discussions with other suppliers cover remaining premises outside rollout plans.
sources.scope_limit: Contract termination does not prove either presence or absence of service at a premises because commercial rollout and replacement arrangements may differ.
sources.attribution: Official GOV.UK HTML; Open Government Licence v3.0 attribution retained.
